subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should same-workspace memory-source agents share one default SQLite store, and if so what migration, session-visibility, and plugin SDK contract must ship with that change?
rationale: This changes persistent memory ownership and cross-agent/session visibility semantics, which automation cannot choose safely from code mechanics alone.

options.title: Redesign contract before merge
options.body: Require a settled shared-store boundary, migration or rebuild-warning path, session visibility proof, and removal or approval of the registry SDK surface before this changes the default store.

options.title: Accept shared workspace as the boundary
options.body: Maintainers can intentionally approve the same-workspace shared DB model, but the PR should then document and own the migration cost, privacy model, and SDK contract.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep the canonical design issue open and avoid landing this branch until the storage and privacy model is ready.

recommendation.title: Redesign contract before merge
recommendation.body: Require a settled shared-store boundary, migration or rebuild-warning path, session visibility proof, and removal or approval of the registry SDK surface before this changes the default store.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history across memory search, session memory, and the SDK extraction touched by this PR.
